q1.question: Est-ce que Compass peut me dire quel 国家 choisir ?
q1.answer: 否. L'outil analyse les 国家 et simule des scénarios, mais la décision finale t'appartient. Nous fournissons l'information, tu fais tes propres choix.

q2.question: Is the data reliable?
q2.answer: We use public sources (corruption indices, tax data, passport rankings). This data is indicative and may change. Always verify with official sources before making important decisions.

q3.question: What's the difference between "My simulation" and "Educational mode"?
q3.answer: "My simulation" (Strategies) analyzes YOUR real situation with YOUR parameters. "Educational mode" has you play a FICTIONAL random character to understand mechanics without personal involvement.

q4.question: Is it free?
q4.answer: 是, l'outil est gratuit. Tu peux créer un compte pour synchroniser tes données entre appareils, mais ce n'est pas obligatoire.

q5.question: Is my personal data protected?
q5.answer: Simulation data stays on your device or in your personal account. We don't sell your data and don't share it with anyone.

q6.question: Can I use this tool for important decisions?
q6.answer: This tool is a starting point for your reflection, not an absolute source of truth. For important decisions (immigration, taxes, health), always consult qualified professionals.

jsonld.a1: Compass est la première plateforme d'aide à la décision pour la relocalisation internationale. Elle analyse 80+ 国家 en profondeur : fiscalité, coût de la vie, visas, qualité de vie et profils compatibles.
jsonld.q2: How does the expat profile test work?
jsonld.a2: Le test rapide évalue vos priorités (fiscalité, qualité de vie, sécurité, opportunités) en 2 minutes. Il vous suggère les 国家 les plus compatibles avec votre profil spécifique, contrairement aux classements génériques.
jsonld.a3: L'accès de base est gratuit : test rapide, exploration des 80+ 国家, comparaison basique. Le plan Premium à 9,90€/mois donne accès aux stratégies de sortie, simulateur fiscal et analyses approfondies.
jsonld.q4: Where does Compass data come from?
jsonld.a4: Data comes from the World Bank, OECD, IMF, Transparency International, Numbeo and government sources. Intelligence is updated regularly via verified sources.
jsonld.q5: Puis-je comparer plusieurs 国家 pour mon expatriation ?
jsonld.a5: 是, l'outil de comparaison permet de comparer jusqu'à 4 国家 simultanément sur fiscalité, coût de la vie, qualité de vie, visas, sécurité et plus, avec des radar charts et exports PDF.
jsonld.q6: How is Compass different from classic expatriation guides?

bias.title: Cognitive Biases
bias.subtitle: The invisible filters of our decisions

s1.title: Introduction
s1.p1: Our brain is an extraordinary machine, capable of processing millions of pieces of information per second. To achieve this, it uses shortcuts — heuristics that allow us to decide quickly.
s1.p2: Ces raccourcis sont précieux dans la vie quotidienne. 五月s ils peuvent devenir des pièges dans les décisions importantes, là où la nuance compte.

s2.title: The most common biases
s2.i1: Confirmation bias: seeking information that confirms what we already believe
s2.i2: Anchoring bias: giving too much importance to the first information received
s2.i3: Availability bias: overestimating what is easily memorable
s2.i4: Survivorship bias: seeing only successes, not silent failures
s2.i5: Status quo bias: preferring not to change, even when suboptimal
s2.i6: Loss aversion: fearing loss more than desiring gain

s3.title: Why it's hard to see
s3.p1: Biases are invisible precisely because they are part of how we think. We can't 'step out' of our brain to observe it from outside.
s3.p2: That's why thinking frameworks, reading grids, and dialogue with other perspectives are so important. They create distance — a space to see what escapes us.

bias.quote: The first step toward clarity is not eliminating biases — it's admitting we have them.

s4.title: What to do?
s4.p1: It's not about eliminating biases — that's impossible. It's about creating conditions where they have less grip on important decisions.
s4.p2: Slow down. Write. Question certainties. Seek divergent opinions. Distinguish what we know from what we assume.

bias.key1: Biases are useful shortcuts — except in complex decisions
bias.key2: We can't eliminate them, but we can create distance
bias.key3: Methodical doubt is a tool, not a weakness

irreversible.title: Irreversible Decisions
irreversible.subtitle: Distinguishing what can be undone from what cannot

s1.title: The uniformity trap
s1.p1: We tend to treat all decisions the same way. Yet some can be cancelled with a few clicks; others commit for years, or forever.
s1.p2: Confusing the two means either hesitating too long on what doesn't matter, or committing too fast on what does.

s2.title: A simple typology
s2.i1: 类型 1 : Irréversibles. Une fois franchies, pas de retour. Exemples : avoir un enfant, révéler un secret, détruire une relation.
s2.i2: 类型 2 : Réversibles avec coût. On peut revenir en arrière, mais ça coûte (temps, argent, énergie). Exemples : changer de 国家, quitter un emploi, acheter un bien.
s2.i3: 类型 3 : Facilement réversibles. Peu de conséquences à annuler. Exemples : tester un outil, modifier un document, reporter une réunion.

irreversible.warning: 警告 : nous sous-estimons souvent le coût de réversibilité. "Je pourrai toujours revenir" est parfois une illusion confortable.

s3.title: Adapting your method
s3.p1: 更多 une décision est irréversible, plus elle mérite du temps, de la réflexion et des perspectives multiples.
s3.p2: Les décisions de 类型 1 demandent une vraie pause. Pas de l'hésitation stérile — mais du temps pour voir ce qu'on ne voit pas encore.

irreversible.key1: 全部es les décisions ne méritent pas le même investissement
irreversible.key2: The cost of reversibility is often underestimated
irreversible.key3: 更多 c'est irréversible, plus ça mérite du temps

control.title: Illusion of Control
control.subtitle: What really depends on us

s1.title: The myth of "anything is possible"
s1.p1: Contemporary culture values agency: "if you want it, you can do it". Sometimes true. Sometimes a cruel lie.
s1.p2: We evolve in systems — economic, social, institutional — that constrain our possibilities. Ignoring them is preparing for disappointment.

s2.title: Three zones to distinguish
s2.i1: Control zone: what depends entirely on me (my actions, my reactions, my effort)
s2.i2: Influence zone: what I can act on, but without guarantee (my relationships, certain opportunities)
s2.i3: Acceptance zone: what escapes me (the market, others' decisions, chance)

s3.title: Why it matters
s3.p1: Confusing these zones generates either frustration (when we fail to control the uncontrollable), or passivity (when we give up acting where we can).
s3.p2: Clarity consists of investing energy where it has grip, and accepting the rest — not by resignation, but by realism.

control.key1: 全部 n'est pas sous notre contrôle — et c'est normal
control.key2: Distinguishing control, influence, and acceptance saves energy

speed.title: Speed vs Haste
speed.subtitle: Acting fast is not acting in urgency

s1.title: Two ways to go fast
s1.p1: Speed can be a strategic advantage. Acting before others, seizing an opportunity, iterating quickly — all this has value.
s1.p2: 五月s il y a une différence entre la vitesse délibérée et la précipitation. L'une est choisie ; l'autre est subie.

s2.title: Signs of haste
s2.i1: No time to ask "is this really urgent?"
s2.i2: Ignoring doubts because we must move forward
s2.i3: Justifying haste by fear of missing out
s2.i4: Unable to clearly explain why now

s3.title: The real question
s3.p1: Before acting fast, ask yourself: "Am I choosing this speed, or am I suffering it?"
s3.p2: Chosen speed is powerful. Suffered haste is dangerous.

speed.key1: Speed can be an asset — if chosen
speed.key2: Haste is often a symptom, not a strategy
speed.key3: Taking 5 minutes to ask the question can avoid 5 months of regret

individual.title: Individual vs System
individual.subtitle: Personal responsibility and structural constraints

s1.title: A false dilemma
s1.p1: On one side, the "anything is possible if you believe" discourse. On the other, systemic fatalism: "the system is against you".
s1.p2: Both are true — and false. Reality is more nuanced: we act in systems that constrain us AND offer possibilities.

s2.title: What the system does
s2.p1: A system defines rules, incentives, obstacles. It rewards certain behaviors and punishes others. It creates easy paths and dead ends.
s2.p2: Ignoring the system means fighting invisible forces. Understanding it means knowing where to place your efforts.

s3.title: What remains for the individual
s3.p1: Even in the most constraining systems, margins remain. Choices. Ways to navigate.
s3.p2: Individual responsibility is not about controlling everything — it's about doing the maximum with what is under our control.

individual.key2: Understanding the system helps navigate it better
individual.key3: Responsibility applies to what depends on us, not the rest

concept.title: The Concept
concept.description: PYRAMIDES est un jeu de stratégie où tu gères des trajectoires de vie. Tu ne choisis pas ton point de départ : tu tires des personnages avec un 国家 de naissance, des traits, et des aspirations. À chaque 'année' de jeu, tu prends des décisions : travailler, étudier, soigner, migrer, entreprendre, construire ton réseau, nourrir tes relations... Le monde bouge, les 国家 ont leurs règles, et la réussite dépend de ta capacité à optimiser sous contrainte.

welcome.title: Bienvenue dans le 四 de la Vie
welcome.content: This game simulates the realities that millions of people experience around the world. This is not fiction — it's a mirror of the real world, with its opportunities and dangers.
welcome.reality: Every mechanic in this game reflects a lived reality. Our goal is prevention and understanding, not fear.

lifeAssignment.title: You don't choose your starting life
lifeAssignment.content: Like in real life, you don't choose where you're born, your starting economic situation, or your initial constraints. The game assigns you a random life — some easier, some very difficult.
lifeAssignment.reality: Naître dans un 国家 stable avec un bon passeport est un privilège. D'autres doivent lutter pour des droits que beaucoup considèrent acquis.
examples: Un Suisse né à Genève vs un Nigérian né à Lagos — mêmes ambitions, opportunités très différentes
Une femme née en Arabie Saoudite vs une née au Canada — libertés fondamentales différentes
Un enfant né dans une famille riche vs une famille pauvre — même 国家, trajectoires différentes

resources.title: Your life resources
resources.content: You manage 6 essential resources: Health, Money, Network, Security, Education and Morale. Every decision affects them. If some drop to zero, consequences can be severe.
resources.reality: In real life, losing your health or network can mean the end of all opportunities. Money alone doesn't protect from everything.
examples: Santé : une maladie chronique change tout le calcul de l'expatriation
Réseau : sans contacts, même les compétences ne suffisent pas
Sécurité : un passeport faible limite drastiquement les options

pyramids.title: Chaque 国家 a son système
pyramids.content: Les 6 types de pyramides représentent comment chaque 国家 fonctionne vraiment. Certains récompensent la compétence, d'autres les connexions, d'autres encore l'extraction de ressources.
pyramids.reality: Comprendre le système d'un 国家 est crucial. Ce qui fonctionne en Allemagne peut être fatal au Cameroun, et vice versa.

events.title: Life sends you events
events.content: Each turn, global and local events affect your resources. Economic crises, opportunities, natural disasters, political changes — you must adapt.
events.reality: Nobody controls everything. Migrants who planned everything can see their plans destroyed by a policy change overnight.
examples: Une crise économique mondiale peut effacer des années d'épargne
Un nouveau gouvernement peut fermer les frontières ou changer les règles du visa

actions.title: Your choices define your trajectory
actions.content: Each turn, you can work, study, network, save, or take risks. Major actions have more impact but carry more risk.
actions.reality: Every choice has an opportunity cost. Studying means less immediate money. Working hard without a network may lead nowhere.

shortcuts.title: Dangerous shortcuts
shortcuts.content: The game offers 'shortcuts' — illegal crossing, undocumented work, fake documents. These options exist because they exist in real life. Consequences can be catastrophic.
shortcuts.reality: Every year, thousands of people die attempting these shortcuts. In Libya, human trafficking is a reality. This game doesn't glorify these choices — it shows their real consequences.
examples: Traversée de la Méditerranée : risque réel de mort, interception, ou esclavage
Faux documents : emprisonnement, déportation, interdiction de retour
Travail au noir : exploitation, absence de protection, vulnérabilité totale

aspirations.title: Your personal goals
aspirations.content: Your character has aspirations — becoming wealthy, living safely, reuniting with family, or simply surviving. Success is measured against YOUR goals, not a universal standard.
aspirations.reality: 'Success' is relative. A refugee who rebuilds their life has accomplished as much as an entrepreneur who becomes a millionaire.

endgame.title: Life summary
endgame.content: At the end, the game evaluates whether you achieved your aspirations, preserved your health, and navigated the system. There's no 'right' way to play — only choices and their consequences.
endgame.reality: This game is a tool for understanding. Whether it helps you appreciate your situation or better understand others', that's its real victory.

universalErrors.title: Universal Errors Library
universalErrors.subtitle: The 10 most costly decision errors. No moralizing, just facts and tools to avoid them.
universalErrors.intro: These errors are not moral failings. They are recurring patterns that cost time, money, and energy. Recognizing them allows you to anticipate them.
universalErrors.simulateDescription: Test a decision related to this error to identify risks before committing.
universalErrors.ctaTitle: Do you recognize one of these errors?
universalErrors.ctaDescription: Run your decision through the prevention filter to identify risks before it's too late.

systemError.name: 错误 de système
systemError.shortDescription: Ignoring the real rules of the system you operate in.
systemError.definition: Acting according to personal expectations rather than the actual rules of the system (tax, legal, social) you're subject to.
systemError.whyItHappens: On projette souvent les règles de son 国家 d'origine ou de son environnement familier sur un nouveau contexte. L'information fiable est difficile à trouver et les systèmes sont complexes.
systemError.timeCost: 6 months to 2 years of procedures or adaptation

metricError.name: 错误 de métrique
metricError.shortDescription: Optimizing the wrong indicator or measuring only what reassures.
metricError.definition: Focusing on superficial indicators (gross salary, prestige) while ignoring metrics that truly matter (quality of life, real cost, progress).
metricError.whyItHappens: Visible metrics are easy to communicate and compare. Important metrics are often invisible or uncomfortable to measure.
metricError.timeCost: Years spent chasing the wrong goal
metricError.moneyCost: Investments in areas that bring nothing

timingError.name: 错误 de timing
timingError.shortDescription: Acting too early, too late, or ignoring system cycles.
timingError.definition: Not accounting for economic, seasonal, or institutional cycles that determine an action's success.
timingError.whyItHappens: Impatience pushes for immediate action. Long cycles are hard to perceive when you're in them.
timingError.energyCost: Frustration of swimming against the current

irreversibilityError.name: 错误 d'irréversibilité
irreversibilityError.shortDescription: Committing to a hard-to-correct decision without testing it.
irreversibilityError.definition: Making a high-commitment decision (marriage, property purchase, permanent expatriation) without a test phase or possible withdrawal.
irreversibilityError.whyItHappens: Social pressure values total commitment. Testing before committing is sometimes seen as lack of confidence.
irreversibilityError.timeCost: Years correcting a mistake or living with it
irreversibilityError.moneyCost: Very high exit costs (divorce, selling at a loss)

hiddenCostError.name: 错误 de coût caché
hiddenCostError.shortDescription: Underestimating real costs beyond the displayed price.
hiddenCostError.definition: Only seeing visible costs (price, salary) while ignoring hidden costs (maintenance, stress, time, lost opportunities).
hiddenCostError.whyItHappens: Sellers and systems minimize hidden costs. Our brain prefers simple numbers to complex calculations.
hiddenCostError.timeCost: Invisible hours of maintenance and management

egoError.name: 错误 d'ego
egoError.shortDescription: Letting status or image guide economic decisions.
egoError.definition: Making decisions based on what you want to project rather than what you actually need.
egoError.whyItHappens: Social status is a fundamental human need. Others' perceptions influence our choices more than we admit.
egoError.moneyCost: Status purchases at the expense of security
egoError.energyCost: Anxiety related to keeping up appearances

environmentError.name: 错误 d'environnement
environmentError.shortDescription: Ignoring the environment's influence on your results.
environmentError.definition: Croire que le succès dépend uniquement de l'effort personnel en ignorant le rôle du contexte (国家, réseau, époque, secteur).
environmentError.whyItHappens: Meritocracy is a dominant narrative. Acknowledging the environment's role can seem to diminish one's merits.
environmentError.timeCost: Years stagnating in the wrong environment
environmentError.moneyCost: Unrealized potential due to poor positioning

narrativeError.name: 错误 de narration
narrativeError.shortDescription: Confusing an inspiring story with an applicable strategy.
narrativeError.definition: Following a narrative (success story, guru advice) without verifying if it applies to your own situation.
narrativeError.whyItHappens: Stories are more memorable than statistics. Survivorship bias makes successes more visible than failures.
narrativeError.moneyCost: Investments in irrelevant training or advice
narrativeError.energyCost: Self-doubt when promised results don't arrive

sunkCost.name: Sunk Cost
sunkCost.shortDescription: 继续 à investir parce qu'on a déjà trop investi.
sunkCost.definition: Pursuing an unfavorable action because you've already committed time, money, or energy you don't want to lose.
sunkCost.whyItHappens: Our brain hates losses. Admitting a past mistake is painful. We hope the situation will improve.
sunkCost.timeCost: Additional years in a dead end
sunkCost.moneyCost: Additional investments to justify previous ones
sunkCost.energyCost: Exhaustion maintaining something that doesn't work

socialProofError.name: 错误 de copie (social proof)
socialProofError.shortDescription: Imitating others without checking if their situation applies to yours.
socialProofError.definition: Following the majority's or admired figures' behavior without analyzing if their constraints and goals are the same.

humanTrafficking.title: Human trafficking
humanTrafficking.description: Human trafficking affects over 40 million people worldwide. Victims are often recruited through false promises of work or study abroad.

stats.1: 更多 de 50 000 personnes victimes de traite identifiées en Europe chaque année
stats.2: 71% of trafficking victims are women and girls

warnings.1: You're asked to hand over your identity documents
warnings.2: Unrealistic promises of salary or living conditions
warnings.3: Request for upfront payment for a "visa" or "work contract"
warnings.4: Isolation from your family and friends
warnings.5: Contract only oral or in a language you don't understand

prevention.1: ALWAYS verify the legal existence of the employer or agency
prevention.2: ALWAYS keep your identity documents with you

prevention.4: Use legal immigration routes even if they take longer

prevention.2: Demand a written contract in your language

warnings.2: Payment request before any official process

prevention.1: ALWAYS consult the official embassy website

stats.4: Amsterdam, Paris, Rome: main exploitation destinations

prevention.3: Talk about ANY offer to your family and friends

healthcareAbroad.description: S'installer à l'étranger sans anticiper les frais de santé peut être désastreux. Les systèmes de santé varient énormément d'un 国家 à l'autre.

warnings.2: Ne pas vérifier les accords de sécurité sociale entre 国家

prevention.1: Get international health insurance BEFORE leaving
prevention.4: Learn about the local healthcare system before leaving
prevention.5: Keep sufficient quantities of essential medications

retirementAbroad.title: Retirement abroad
retirementAbroad.description: Prendre sa retraite dans un 国家 au coût de la vie plus bas est tentant, mais comporte des risques souvent sous-estimés.

stats.1: De nombreux retraités français vivent au 二oc, Portugal, Thaïlande

prevention.1: Test with extended stays before settling
prevention.2: Keep an address and ties in France
prevention.4: Check tax and social security agreements
prevention.5: Keep part of your savings in accessible euros

expatBubble.title: Expat bubble trap
expatBubble.description: Living among expats without integrating can lead to isolation, high living costs, and a superficial experience.

prevention.3: Plan periods of stability between your moves
